skill.name: perf-fullstack-engineer
skill.description: Guides full-stack performance testing, monitoring, bottleneck analysis, capacity planning, optimization, and implementation across frontend, backend, APIs, databases, and DevOps.
skill.summary: Plan performance tests, diagnose bottlenecks, optimize systems, and structure full-stack delivery workflows.
skill.author: zl2023github

security_audit.summary: The skill is readable Markdown guidance with no executable package, prompt injection, credential collection, obfuscation, or covert data transfer. Static alerts primarily misread Markdown backticks, Chinese text, placeholders, localhost URLs, and documented developer commands as dangerous behavior.

remediation.issue: Load tests and diagnostic commands can affect systems when an agent follows the examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval and target authorization before running tests, changing database settings, or collecting production profiles.

remediation.issue: The WebPageTest example places an API key placeholder in a command URL.
remediation.suggestion: Show secret-safe invocation through an environment variable and warn users about shell history, process lists, and request logs.

content.value_statement: Full-stack teams often lack a repeatable way to measure performance and locate bottlenecks. This skill provides testing workflows, diagnostic commands, optimization guidance, and report structures.
actual_capabilities: Defines TPS, QPS, latency percentiles, concurrency, error rate, throughput, and resource targets.
Designs baseline, load, stress, endurance, peak, and capacity tests.
Provides a k6 example and selection guidance for JMeter, Locust, wrk, Vegeta, and Apache Bench.
Guides diagnosis across hosts, JVMs, databases, applications, containers, and monitoring platforms.
Covers frontend, backend, API, database, architecture, deployment, and operations workflows.
Structures performance reports with environments, scenarios, trends, bottlenecks, recommendations, and conclusions.
limitations: The skill contains guidance only, with no executable files, integrations, or automated result parser.
Commands, URLs, thresholds, and test data are examples that require project-specific adaptation.
Results depend on representative environments, workloads, monitoring coverage, and repeated measurements.
Third-party tools must be installed, and infrastructure access must be authorized.

use_cases.title: Establish a Performance Baseline
use_cases.description: Define service targets, select test scenarios, and produce a repeatable baseline before a release.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Slow Application
use_cases.description: Correlate latency, resource, runtime, database, and application signals to prioritize likely bottlenecks.

use_cases.title: Plan Capacity for Growth
use_cases.description: Model peak traffic, identify system limits, and organize scaling recommendations with measurable acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a performance baseline for [service]. Use [traffic profile], [latency target], [error target], and [environment]. List assumptions and required metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Load Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [tool] load test for [workflow]. Include stages, data preparation, checks, thresholds, monitoring, cleanup, and a safe execution sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these performance results: [results]. Correlate application, host, database, runtime, and network evidence. Rank hypotheses and propose verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Capacity Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a capacity plan for [system] at [forecast load]. Estimate limits, identify architecture risks, compare scaling options, and define regression gates.

output_examples.input: Define a baseline for a checkout API expecting 200 requests per second.
output_examples.output: Target 200 requests per second with P95 below 500 milliseconds and errors below 0.1 percent. Measure CPU, memory, database latency, and saturation.

output_examples.input: Diagnose rising P99 latency while CPU remains below 50 percent.
output: Primary hypotheses: database lock waits, connection pool saturation, external dependency latency, or garbage collection pauses.
Next checks: correlate traces, pool metrics, slow queries, lock activity, dependency timing, and runtime pause data.

output_examples.input: Outline a performance report after an optimization.
output_examples.output: Compare the same workload before and after the change. Show latency percentiles, throughput, errors, resource use, remaining bottlenecks, and release recommendations.

best_practices: Confirm target ownership, isolate the test environment, and obtain approval before generating load.
Warm the system, monitor every layer, increase load gradually, and repeat comparable tests.
Base conclusions on correlated metrics and document assumptions, environment differences, and data limitations.
anti_patterns: Do not run stress tests against production or third-party systems without explicit authorization.
Do not optimize from averages alone; inspect percentiles, errors, saturation, and resource trends.
Do not change multiple variables between baseline and comparison runs.

faq.question: Does this skill run performance tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows, examples, diagnostics, and report structures. Execution requires installed tools, adapted targets, and user authorization.

faq.question: Which load-testing tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers k6, JMeter, Locust, wrk, Vegeta, and Apache Bench, with guidance for selecting tools by scenario.

faq.question: Can it analyze database performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers query plans, slow queries, active sessions, locks, indexing, connection pools, and common MySQL and PostgreSQL diagnostics.

faq.question: Does it support frontend performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Lighthouse, browser diagnostics, code splitting, lazy loading, virtual lists, image optimization, caching, and content delivery networks.

faq.question: Can I use its thresholds without changes?
faq.answer: No. Example thresholds are starting points. Set targets from business requirements, service objectives, historical baselines, and environment constraints.

faq.question: Is production load testing recommended?
faq.answer: No. Use an isolated representative environment unless your organization has an approved production testing process with safeguards and monitoring.
